summary: The comment at shaders.c:139-143 says the shared last slot of seen[] costs 'a suppression nobody will miss' by aggregating vendor codes. The code does the opposite: the scan at :155 runs i over 0..ARRAY_SIZE(seen)-2 (slots 0-6 only), so a miss leaves i == 7, and :160-163 then re-keys that slot and sets count = 0 whenever the resident enum differs. Two distinct enums alternating in slot 7 each reset the other's count and print with occurrence=1 on every single load. The shared slot does not cost a suppression, it removes suppression entirely for whatever lands in it. Confirmed by compiling the live sliced block against the selftest's stubs: seven distinct enums -> 7 lines (correct); 200 alternating loads through slot 7 -> 200 lines, every one occurrence=1; 100 loads of one enum resident alone in slot 7 -> 3 lines (correct). The defect is specifically the alternation.
scenario: A device run in which eight or more distinct GL error enums occur over the process lifetime -- the desktop-GL set is exactly eight, and a GLES driver reaching six standard codes plus two vendor codes is the same arithmetic. Slots 0-6 fill with the first seven; the eighth and any further code then alternate through slot 7 and every shader load that drains one emits a line. That is the logcat flood the power-of-ten rule exists to prevent, arriving in precisely the badly-broken-renderer case where a readable log matters most, and reporting occurrence=1 for each so the log also understates the count.
remediation: Either make the shared slot genuinely aggregate (scan 0..ARRAY_SIZE(seen)-1 and, on a miss at the last slot, keep counting under a sentinel rather than re-keying), or size seen[] so no slot is shared and delete the sentence at :141-143. Whichever is chosen, comment and code must agree and the selftest must exercise it -- see L1.
evidence: hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/gl/shaders.c:139-143, :144-147, :155-164; probe build of the anchor-sliced block against docs/testing/glerr_report_selftest.c's stubs, output 'after seven distinct enums: lines=7' / '200 alternating loads into the shared slot: lines=200' / '100 loads of ONE enum resident in the shared slot: lines=3'.

summary: Both factual premises the suppression is sized from are false. (a) shaders.c:123-124 says the Android drain 'left the shipping renderer with no error-reporting path at all', and the PR body repeats it. shaders.c already contains three ungated Android GL-error reporters: android_log_shader_stage_errors (:49, called :1025 and :1037), android_log_apply_uniform_entry_errors (:59, called :901) and android_log_uniform_update_errors (:70, called :944). None is behind DEBUG_NV2A_GL; all print 'GL error 0x%X ...' to logcat under the same hakuX tag, one line per error, with no suppression, and :944 fires per uniform per apply. NOTES.md:127 calls these 'debug-logging-gated', which is wrong for the shaders.c ones. (b) shaders.c:131 says 'A shader load happens many times a frame', the sole justification for the power-of-ten machinery. pgraph_gl_shader_load_from_memory has one caller, :1003, guarded by !binding->initialized; initialized is cleared only in shader_cache_entry_init (:700) when an LRU node is freshly claimed, against a 50*1024 = 51200 entry cache (:746-752). It runs once per distinct shader state per run -- hundreds of times, front-loaded -- not many times a frame.
scenario: The suppression built on (b) discards exactly what the feature exists to publish. An error found pending at between 2 and 9 shader loads prints one line, reporting occurrence=1 and the FIRST load's shader hash; the other loads and their hashes never appear. At the real call frequency most counts live in 1..9, so in the common case the counter is printed once and never updated and a recurring pending error is indistinguishable in the log from a single one -- while the docstring and NOTES.md:125-126 say the shader hash is the point of the line. (a) narrows the window further: update_shader_uniforms runs on EVERY pgraph_gl_bind_shaders (:1039, reached by both the goto update_uniforms fast path and the full path) and calls apply_uniform_updates twice (:962, :974), each of which drains and prints the whole backlog at :901. So when a later cache-missing bind reaches :1003 the backlog is at most one draw deep: the new report can only see errors raised since the previous bind's uniform updates, not 'whatever ran before the load' as :119-120 states. An error raised and already reported by :901 leaves no [glerr] line at all, so NOTES.md's reading of an empty grep as 'no GL error was pending at any shader load in the run' is a statement about that narrow window and will be read by the next lane as a statement about the run.
remediation: Correct both claims in the docstring, NOTES.md and the PR body: Android already reports GL errors ungated at :901/:944/:1025/:1037, and this change adds a report at the one Android site that was silent. Then re-decide the suppression on the true frequency -- at one call per cache miss, printing every occurrence is affordable and keeps the per-load shader hash, which is the diagnostic; if suppression is kept, say what it protects against, since it is not the frame rate. Drop '(debug-logging-gated)' for the shaders.c helpers and state that an empty [glerr] grep does not mean the run was GL-error-free.

summary: NOTES.md is added at the branch root. origin/master:docs/testing/jobs/roles/lane.md:48-53 requires docs/lanes/<lane name>/NOTES.md and says 'Not the branch root', with the reason; origin/master:docs/lanes/notespath/NOTES.md is the record of the lane that changed it ('the first lane to fold landed one on master, after which every fold conflicted on that exact path'). Master carries seventeen docs/lanes/<name>/ directories today and no root NOTES.md. This worktree is 150 commits behind and its local roles/lane.md still says 'branch root', so the lane followed the rule it was given; the consequence is a property of the fold, not of the intent.
scenario: fold.sh's resolve_root_notes fires only when root NOTES.md is an UNMERGED path. Master has none, so folding #128 is a clean add and the guard never runs: lane.glerr86's notes land at the repository root permanently. The next lane still carrying a root NOTES.md then conflicts, resolve_root_notes fires, moves the NEWCOMER's copy to docs/lanes/<lane>/ and keeps MASTER's -- glerr86's -- at the root. That is the steady state the notespath lane was opened to remove, reseeded by this PR and thereafter permanent, with one lane's record occupying a repository-root path and this lane's notes absent from the set where every other lane's are readable.
remediation: git mv NOTES.md docs/lanes/glerr86/NOTES.md and update the PR body's Files: line. One commit, no content change.
evidence: git ls-tree origin/master (no root NOTES.md); git ls-tree origin/master docs/lanes/ (17 entries incl. notespath, cloud-109, cloud-110); origin/master:docs/testing/jobs/roles/lane.md:48-53; origin/master:docs/lanes/notespath/NOTES.md.

summary: seen[] is the only state in the change and its capacity behaviour is the only way the block can misbehave (M1), but the harness uses five distinct enums across its whole run -- GL_INVALID_OPERATION, GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY, GL_INVALID_VALUE, GL_INVALID_ENUM and 0x8000 -- so slots 5, 6 and the shared slot 7 are never reached in either build. Eighteen legs pass and none of them could have caught M1. Separately, and correctly flagged by the lane itself, the two suppression legs pass vacuously against the silent build; the harness says so where they are written, which is the right handling, noted here only so pass 2 does not count sixteen discriminating legs as eighteen.
scenario: M1 shipped with a green 18/18 selftest in both header sets and a falsifier that failed by name on ten legs. The suite reads as thorough coverage of the block while leaving its only stateful path untested, so the next change to seen[] will be made against the same false assurance.
remediation: Add a leg that drives eight or more distinct enums and asserts the total line count for a repeated alternating pair, alongside whichever fix M1 takes.

summary: The PR body's 'What is not proved' says 'This lane has no NDK, no device and no arm64 build', NOTES.md:55-58 repeats it, and the header line reads 'Needs NDK: no to review, yes to build the arm'. True of the worktree and not true of the PR. .github/workflows/android.yml runs on every pull_request, installs ndk;29.0.14206865 and runs ./gradlew assembleDebug, which drives android/app/src/main/cpp/CMakeLists.txt through externalNativeBuild (android/app/build.gradle.kts:119-122); that CMake build compiles XEMU_CORE_SOURCES into xemu_core, which includes hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/gl/shaders.c with __ANDROID__ defined against the real GLES header set. The Android check on this head completed SUCCESS at 2026-09-19T06:27:32Z. Not a defect -- the opposite: the check the lane names as missing has already been performed, and it discharges the <android/log.h>, ARRAY_SIZE and GLES-header questions the selftest could only approximate.
scenario: Left as written, the next lane inherits a 'we have no NDK, so the Android build is unverified' caveat that the repository stopped being subject to when android.yml landed, and either repeats the caveat or spends a dispatch re-establishing what CI already reports on every push.
remediation: Replace the caveat with what is actually unproven: the block compiles and links for arm64 under the shipping NDK (CI, this head); what remains unverified is only that a [glerr] line reaches logcat on a device and that the report fires on a real pending error.
evidence: .github/workflows/android.yml (pull_request trigger, sdkmanager ndk;29.0.14206865, gradlew assembleDebug); android/app/build.gradle.kts:119-122; android/app/src/main/cpp/CMakeLists.txt XEMU_CORE_SOURCES / add_library(xemu_core STATIC ...); gh pr view 128 --json statusCheckRollup -> Android/build SUCCESS 2026-09-19T06:27:32Z.
